messages:
Mike: quick probe—ran layerwise clamp+skip sweep for new-open model (gpt-neox-20b-rlf). AWQ vs GPTQ vs INT8 baseline on our internal WebBench subset. initial takeaway: AWQ with surgical clamp on layers 11,18 reduced tail activations and cut perplexity delta from +3.2% to +0.6%.

Sophia: nice. what's the eval set and seed? any examples of regressions that remained?

Mike: eval set = webbench-v1-mini (10k samples), seed=42. Most regressions were on long-context Q/A where prefix kv-decay matters. example small table:

```
mode    | PPL delta | top1-acc delta | notes
GPTQ    | +3.2%     | -1.1%          | layer18 spike
INT8    | +4.8%     | -2.4%          | multiple layers
AWQ     | +1.9%     | -0.6%          | improved with clamp
AWQ+skip| +0.6%     | -0.2%          | skipped layer18
```

Raj: what exact clamp params did you use? per-channel clamp or global? and how did you pick skip candidate?

Mike: per-channel clamp on activations post-attn (k/v). clamp_scale = 1.8 for high-variance channels, fallback global clamp_scale=2.4. skip list chosen by scanning per-layer z-score of max activation (threshold 5.5) and manual triage. command used:

```
./bakeoff --model gpt-neox-20b-rlf --modes awq,gptq,int8 --per-layer-scan --clamp-policy per_channel --clamp-scale 1.8 --skip-threshold 5.5 --seed 42
```

Claire: any latency/cost tradeoffs? skipping layers likely increases runtime since fallback to fp16 right?

Mike: good point—skip = force FP16 exec for that layer, so +6–9% p50 latency on dedicated GPUs. but cost/unit lower than full-GPTQ fallback because we only FP16 for 1–2 layers. overall throughput hit small vs accuracy win.
